newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin reprimands lower house of parliament.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin reprimands lower house of parliament.

text.p: MOSCOW, April 9 (Russia) - Russian President Boris Yeltsin reprimanded the opposition-dominated lower house of parliament on Wednesday for overstepping the constitution with its frequent political judgements on domestic and foreign policy.

"In 1996 alone the lower house adopted several hundred resolutions containing a political evaluation of the events in the country," Yeltsin said in a letter to Gennady Seleznyov, chairman of the State Duma lower chamber.

"It is worth pointing out that most of the documents concerned Russia's domestic and foreign policies, which are the domain of the president under the constitution," said the letter, published by the presidential press service.
Yeltsin said the approval of such resolutions discredited the Duma.

The 66-year-old president also scolded the Duma on Tuesday, saying it should prepare legislation more professionally. He told Seleznyov he had recently been forced to reject three out of every four draft laws sent to him by the lower chamber.
Yeltsin has been reprimanding top officials and state bodies in the last few weeks to reassert his authority since his return from a long asbence with illness.

He has said he is ready to take on parliament if it picks a fight, reviving memories of how he dissolved the previous parliament in 1993 and then used tanks to crush a rebellion by hardline parliamentarians. Such a confrontation is unlikely now.
